items.name: mockio-theme
items.title: Mockio tokens
items.description: Both themes as CSS variables, the Tailwind v4 theme (theme.css), the Tailwind v3 preset, tokens.json and the base stylesheet with the component classes.
items.docs: Mockio is dark by default. With shadcn's cssVars, light is :root and dark is .dark, so add class="dark" to <html> for Mockio's default look. Or skip the cssVars and import mockio/tokens/theme.css (Tailwind v4) or the preset in mockio/tokens/tailwind-preset.js (Tailwind v3).

items.title: Mockio contracts

items.name: action
items.title: Action
items.description: The button. One primary per view, in the accent; everything else steps down in tone.

contract.name: Action
contract.summary: The button. One primary per view, in the accent; everything else steps down in tone.

children.description: The label. Starts with a verb and says what happens, not what the button is.

tone.description: How loud the button is. Picks the fill, the ink and the press depth.

values.solid: The one primary action of the view. Accent fill, white ink, a darker edge it sinks into on press.
values.neutral: A confident secondary next to a primary, or the primary on a surface that is already accent-heavy.
values.quiet: A secondary at the same volume as the panel it sits on: a hairline and no fill colour, for the rare errand beside the loud action. It scales on press, because it has no edge to sink into.
values.glass: Over video or imagery, where a solid fill would cover the picture. Translucent, blurred.
values.ghost: Tertiary actions: cancel, skip, a quiet secondary in a toolbar.

withArrow.description: Adds a trailing arrow that nudges forward on hover. Only for the main path forward; it mirrors in right-to-left documents.

type.description: The native button type. Defaults to button so an Action inside a form never submits by accident; pass submit on the form's own button.

disabled.description: Greys the button and removes it from pointer events. Prefer explaining why next to it over a silent disabled state.

className.description: Extra classes, appended. For layout (width, margin) — not for restyling the tone.

onClick.description: Native click handler. Fires on pointer click, `Enter` and `Space`.

slots.name: children
slots.description: Text, optionally preceded by a 16px lucide icon with aria-hidden.

states.name: default
states.description: Resting fill for the tone.

states.name: hover
states.description: solid brightens 10%; neutral dims to 90%; quiet, glass and ghost take the lifted surface. Only on devices that can hover.

states.name: pressed
states.description: solid, neutral and glass translate down by their edge height (4px / 3px) and lose the edge; quiet has no edge, so it scales to 97% instead. All answer in 75ms.

states.name: focus-visible
states.description: 2px accent ring with a 2px offset in the page colour.

states.name: disabled
states.description: solid becomes the neutral lifted grey with faint ink and no edge; quiet dims to 70%; the other tones drop to 40% opacity. No pointer events.

motion: Press: transform and shadow in 75ms with the press ease-out (cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)); release in 150ms.
Arrow: translates 2px toward where it points on hover, 200ms.
Reduced motion: the press is instant; colour and opacity changes still run.

accessibility.role: button (native <button>)

keyboard.effect: Moves focus to the button; the focus ring appears.
Activates on release; shows the pressed state while held.

aria.note: Required only when the label is an icon alone. A visible text label is always preferred.
The trailing arrow is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.
Use aria-disabled instead of disabled when the button must stay focusable to explain why it is unavailable.

accessibility.reducedMotion: Transforms are instant under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce (the system's global rule); the colour change on press remains so the press is still acknowledged.
accessibility.contrast: solid: accent-ink on accent ≥ 5:1 in both themes. neutral: surface-base on cream-bright ≥ 15:1. ghost: cream-dim on surface ≥ 4.5:1 (cream at 0.85).
accessibility.focus: focus-ring: 2px accent ring, 2px offset in surface-base. Visible only for keyboard focus (focus-visible).
accessibility.targetSize: ≥ 40px tall at the default padding (py-2.5 + 16px line); add w-full on phones for primary actions.
accessibility.screenReader: Announced as its text label and the role button. The arrow is not announced.

voice: Start with a verb, in the imperative, tú form in Spanish: "Ensayar", "Sube tu tesis", "Ver mi acta".
Sentence case. No final period. No exclamation marks.
Say the outcome, not the mechanism: "Ver mi informe" rather than "Enviar".
Free things say so in the label when price is the obstacle: "Sube tu tesis gratis".
limits: 1–4 words; ≤ 28 characters so it stays on one line at 320px.

when: Any action the user takes on purpose: start, save, send, confirm, open a flow.
The single most important next step of a screen (tone solid, often withArrow).

whenNot.situation: Navigating to another page as plain navigation
whenNot.instead: a link styled as a link (<a>), with the Action wrapped inside it only when the destination is a step forward.

whenNot.situation: Choosing one option among several
whenNot.instead: a radio group with 2–5 options, each with its own label.

whenNot.situation: A destructive action with no undo
whenNot.instead: an Action that asks for confirmation first, so a stray tap does nothing.

whenNot.situation: Toggling a setting on and off
whenNot.instead: a native checkbox (<input type="checkbox">) with its own label.

do: One solid Action per view; demote the rest to neutral, quiet or ghost.
Put the primary on the right of a pair on desktop and first in the stack on mobile.
Explain a disabled Action in text next to it.
dont: Don't put two solid Actions side by side — the user has to read both to know which matters.
Don't restyle the tone with className colours; add a tone to the contract instead.
Don't use withArrow on secondary or destructive actions.

i18n.rtl: The trailing arrow mirrors (rtl:-scale-x-100) and its hover nudge reverses; the label aligns by the document direction.
i18n.textExpansion: The pill grows with its label and wraps only inside a w-full container; keep labels short enough to stay on one line in Portuguese and German.
i18n.formatting: None: the label is the caller's text.

behaviour: Same size at every width; on phones the primary action usually takes w-full via className.
Pairs stack vertically below 360px, primary first.

designTool.placement: Anywhere an action is taken: forms, cards, toolbars, page headers. Never more than one solid per view.

differences: Defaults type to "button" so it never submits a form by accident; the app's copy relies on the native default (submit).

The press depth differs. This copy is the flat one: the button has no bottom edge and the press is a 3% scale, in every tone. The system's solid, neutral and glass carry an edge the face sinks into (`active:translate-y-[4px]`, `active:translate-y-[3px]`). The hover is a touch brighter in the system (`hover:brightness-110`) than in the product's copy (`hover:brightness-105`), and the glass tone's edge carries the 3px key the copy does not (`shadow-[inset_0_0_0_1px_var(--line),0_3px_0_var(--line-strong)]` against the copy's `shadow-[inset_0_0_0_1px_var(--line)]`). The edge also goes away when the button is disabled (`disabled:shadow-none`), which the flat copy has no need of. The quiet tone is the one that agrees on both sides: a hairline, no edge, and a 3% scale on press.

changes: The contract now names the class names of the difference: the system's press translates and the product's copy scales, and the hover and the glass edge differ too. Nothing changes for a screen.

Nothing changes for a screen: the alternatives are named in plain words now — a link, a radio group, an Action that asks for confirmation first, a native checkbox — because the system has no component for them.
New tone: quiet — a hairline on the card surface, for the rare errand that must not compete with the loud action. The product's copy already had it; the contract now says so.
The press of the quiet tone is a 3% scale rather than a translate: without an edge there is nothing to sink into.
First documented version, extracted from the product.

items.name: backdrop
items.title: Backdrop
items.description: The decorative field behind marketing heroes: slow drifting light, grain and a scrim, all CSS, and the stand-in for footage when there is none.

contract.name: Backdrop
contract.summary: The decorative field behind marketing heroes: slow drifting light, grain and a scrim, all CSS, and the stand-in for footage when there is none.

variant.description: How much light. Picks the number of lights and how far they sit from the frame.

values.hero: The full field: the pale lift from below, the navy across the top-left and a third, fainter light on the right.
values.section: A quieter field for mid-page: the lift and the navy pushed further out of frame, no third light.

still.description: Renders the same composition with no drift. For contexts that must not move — a video's poster frame, a print, a screenshot. Reduced motion stills it without this prop.

className.description: Extra classes on the layer, appended: a z-index, or a rounded corner when the parent does not clip. Not for colour.

states.name: default
states.description: The lights drift on 34s, 46s and 58s loops (the section variant runs the first two). Nothing on top of it appears to move.
states.trigger: Initial render, still={false}, no reduced-motion preference.

states.name: still
states.description: The same composition with no drift class: each light at rest in its place, at scale 1 and full opacity.
states.trigger: still={true}, or prefers-reduced-motion: reduce at mount.

motion: Three CSS loops from the preset: drift-slow (34s, translate + scale + opacity), drift-wide (46s, translate + scale) and drift-counter (58s, translate + scale + opacity), all cubic-bezier(0.45, 0, 0.55, 1), infinite.
Only transform and opacity animate, on blurred layers the GPU composites, so the drift never triggers layout or paint.
The periods are long on purpose: a minute is slow enough that text on top never seems to move.
Reduced motion: no animation class is applied at all (see accessibility.reducedMotion).

accessibility.role: none — a presentational layer, aria-hidden

aria.note: Always set. The field carries no information.
Not ARIA, but the same promise for the pointer: clicks and taps go through to the content above.

accessibility.reducedMotion: The component calls framer-motion's useReducedMotion() and, when the user asks for reduced motion, applies no drift class — it renders exactly as still={true}, with no app-level MotionConfig needed. The preference is read when the component mounts; a change mid-visit is caught by the package stylesheet's reduced-motion block (src/styles.css), which ends every animation after 0.01ms.
accessibility.contrast: Decorative, so it has no contrast requirement of its own; it is built so that light ink over it holds AA anywhere. At its brightest point — both pale lights at full strength under the 10% middle of the scrim, about rgb(69 69 69) before grain — cream-bright text is 9.2:1 and cream-dim 6.9:1. Dark ink never goes on it. On the light theme .backdrop-field dims the whole layer to 28%.
accessibility.focus: Never focusable.
accessibility.screenReader: Nothing. Assistive technology skips the whole layer; whatever sits on top is read normally.

voice: The field has no copy. What sits on it is a hero: a short line in the product's voice, not marketing fluff — "Sustenta antes de sustentar."
The field is atmosphere, not a picture of the product. When there is footage, show the footage.
limits: Copy on top: a headline and one supporting sentence; long reading text belongs on a plain surface.
examples: Un jurado de 3 que leyó tu tesis te pregunta por voz, repregunta como el de verdad y te deja un acta de 0 a 20.

when: Behind a marketing hero when there is no footage, or underneath footage while it loads.
A mid-page marketing section that needs light rather than a flat ground (variant section).

whenNot.situation: Any signed-in screen: the thesis workspace, a rehearsal, an acta, settings
whenNot.instead: the surface tokens (surface-deep, a Panel). Nothing decorative competes with the sentence someone is reading while nervous.

whenNot.situation: There is real footage for the hero
whenNot.instead: the footage itself, over a Backdrop that stands in while it loads.

whenNot.situation: Behind long reading text, a form or a pricing table
whenNot.instead: a plain surface (Section on surface-deep). The drift and the grain cost legibility exactly where it is needed.

whenNot.situation: A section on the light theme that wants a soft tint
whenNot.instead: surface-deep or accent-soft. On a light page the field dims to a hint of itself, by design.

do: Give it a positioned parent that clips: relative isolate overflow-hidden.
Give the parent a dark ground (bg-black, or on-media with bg-surface-base); the field paints light, not a ground.
Put the copy above it with relative z-10.
Pass still when the field is under something that is not moving either (a paused video, a print).
dont: Don't put dark ink on it, or drop it on a light section to make a grey wash.
Don't stack two Backdrops, or add your own grain: it already has some.
Don't use it inside the app.

related.name: Section
related.difference: Owns a marketing section's rhythm and ground; Backdrop is the light inside one.

related.name: Panel
related.difference: A surface that holds content; Backdrop holds nothing and sits behind.

i18n.rtl: Does not mirror. The lights are placed physically (navy top-left, third light right) because they are a composition, not a reading direction.
i18n.textExpansion: No text of its own. It fills its parent, so longer copy on top makes the parent taller and the field follows.
i18n.formatting: None: the component renders no text, numbers or dates.

behaviour: Fills its positioned parent (absolute inset-0) at every width and clips to it.
The lights are sized in vmax, the viewport and not the parent, so the field keeps its proportions from a 320px phone to a wide desktop; a narrow frame on a wide screen shows a crop of it.

designTool.placement: As the first child of a marketing hero or section that is relative, isolate, overflow-hidden and dark. Content goes above it with relative z-10. Never inside the app shell.

differences: The pale lights read rgb(var(--cream) / α) instead of the literal rgba(222,219,200,α) — the first palette's warm cream. They are now the current ink, #F5F5F7, a touch cooler.
The layer carries on-media, so --cream resolves to the dark ink inside it in both themes and the lights stay light on the light theme.
The navy (4 33 46), which has no token, is one named constant instead of two literals; the stale "Velorah" name is gone.
Calls useReducedMotion() itself and applies no drift under reduced motion; the app's copy relies on index.css and on its own video hero passing still.
Adds className.

changes: Nothing changes for a screen: the alternatives are named in plain words now — the surface tokens, the footage itself, a plain surface — because the system has no component for them.
First documented version, extracted from the product.
Cream literals moved to the --cream token; the navy kept as a documented constant.
Reduced motion handled in the component.

items.name: badge
items.title: Badge
items.description: A small pill with a status in words — the mode of a call, a setting in force — and, when live, a breathing dot.

contract.name: Badge
contract.summary: A small pill with a status in words — the mode of a call, a setting in force — and, when live, a breathing dot.

children.description: The status in 1–3 words, optionally led by a 12px icon with aria-hidden. The words carry the meaning; nothing else does.

tone.description: Whether the status is a standing fact or something happening right now.

values.neutral: A fact about the screen: the mode ("Práctica"), a setting in force ("Modo estrés").
values.live: Something in progress at this moment ("Conectando", the interviewer's turn). Prepends an accent dot that breathes.

role.description: Native role, spread onto the span. Pass "status" when the text changes in place and the change should be announced politely.

className.description: Extra classes, appended. For layout (margin, self-alignment) — not for recolouring the pill.

slots.name: children
slots.description: Text, optionally preceded by a 12px (h-3 w-3) lucide icon with aria-hidden.

states.name: default
states.description: The lifted surface pill with cream-dim text; the live tone adds the accent dot before the text.

motion: Live dot: opacity breathes 1 → 0.35 → 1 over 2s on an in-out curve (cubic-bezier(0.45, 0, 0.55, 1)), for as long as the tone is live. A breath rather than a blink, so it can sit beside text someone is reading.
Reduced motion: the dot does not animate and stays at full opacity. The animation class is behind Tailwind's motion-safe: variant, so the component carries its own prefers-reduced-motion check.
Nothing else moves; switching tone swaps the dot in and out without a transition.

accessibility.role: generic (native <span>); status when the consumer passes role="status"

aria.note: The live dot is decoration and is hidden from assistive technology; the words say what is happening.
Add it when the text changes in place and the change matters, like the call's turn counter. Leave it off fixed labels such as "Práctica", or every render is announced.
A leading icon passed in children must carry aria-hidden; the text names the status.

accessibility.reducedMotion: The live dot stays still at full opacity: its animation only applies under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference (motion-safe:). No provider is needed, and a change of the setting applies at once.
accessibility.contrast: Text: cream-dim on surface-lift is ≥ 9.2:1 in both themes over any surface (tightest: the light theme on surface-deep, 9.21:1). The dot is decorative (accent on the lifted pill, 2.8–5.1:1) and is never the only signal.
accessibility.focus: Not focusable.
accessibility.screenReader: Read as its text, inline. The dot is not announced, so "live" reaches a screen reader only through the words — write a status ("Conectando"), not just a name.

voice: A noun or a short status, sentence case, no period: "Práctica", "Modo estrés", "Turno 3 de 8".
Something in progress may be a gerund: "Conectando". No ellipsis — the live dot already says it is ongoing.
Numbers as digits: "Turno 3 de 8".
limits: 1–3 words, ≤ 20 characters. A badge that wraps is a sentence that wants to be body text.

when: A short fact about the current screen that the user is not changing right now: the mode of a call, a setting in force.
A status happening at this moment, with tone live: the call connecting, the interviewer's turn.

whenNot.situation: Something the user can press or toggle
whenNot.instead: Action (ghost), or a radio group. A Badge is not focusable and has no press.

whenNot.situation: Marking an option as part of the paid plan
whenNot.instead: PremiumMark.

whenNot.situation: A message about what just happened
whenNot.instead: Notice.

whenNot.situation: A score or how far along something is
whenNot.instead: Meter, which reports a proportion.

whenNot.situation: Something loading, with nothing to say yet
whenNot.instead: a sentence that names what is loading.

do: Say the state in words; let the dot only add "right now".
One live badge per view at most.
Add role="status" when the text changes in place.
dont: Don't use a Badge as a button or a filter chip.
Don't make every badge live.
Don't recolour it to mean error or success.

related.name: PremiumMark
related.difference: Marks one option as paid, with a crown; Badge states a status in words.

related.name: Eyebrow
related.difference: Places a whole block above its heading; Badge describes one item or the current screen.

i18n.rtl: The dot leads the text in reading order, so it sits on the right in Arabic and Hebrew. A leading icon follows the same order; nothing is mirrored.
i18n.textExpansion: The pill grows with its text. Portuguese and German statuses run about as long ("Modo estresse", "Stressmodus"); a label too long for its row wraps inside the pill, which is the sign to shorten it.
i18n.formatting: None inside the component: a counter such as "Turno 3 de 8" arrives already formatted by the caller.

behaviour: The same size at every width.
A row of badges is the caller's flex row; give it flex-wrap so the badges drop to a second line on a 320px phone instead of overflowing.

designTool.placement: In a page header's actions, beside a title, or at the top of a card. Several sit in a flex row with gap-2 or gap-3.

differences: Accepts className and native span attributes (role, id, data-*); the app's copy takes children and tone only.
The live dot animates only under `motion-safe:animate-live`; the app's copy writes `animate-live` and relies on the global reduced-motion stylesheet to stop it.
The live dot is `shrink-0`, so it keeps its size when the label wraps; the app's copy does not hold its size.

changes: The contract now names the class names of the difference: the system's dot animates under motion-safe and the product's copy writes the plain animation.
Nothing changes for a screen: the alternatives are named in plain words now — a radio group, a Meter, a sentence that names what is loading — because the system has no component for them.
First documented version, extracted from the product.

items.name: check-item
items.title: CheckItem
items.description: One row of a checklist of what a plan or an offer includes: a check in the accent, then the words.

contract.name: CheckItem
contract.summary: One row of a checklist of what a plan or an offer includes: a check in the accent, then the words.

children.description: What is included, as a short phrase. Wrapped in one span, so inline emphasis or a link stays part of the sentence.

className.description: Extra classes, appended. For spacing or a grid span — not for the ink or the check's colour.

slots.name: children
slots.description: A phrase of text; inline elements (<strong>, a link) are fine. No block content and no second icon.

states.name: default
states.description: A 16px check in accent-text aligned to the first line, then the text in cream-dim.

motion: None. A checklist enters with the card around it; rows do not stagger on their own.

accessibility.role: listitem (native <li>) — the consumer supplies the <ul> or <ol>

aria.note: The check is decoration and is not announced on every row.
Say what the checks mean in text before the list — a <dt>, a heading or a paragraph such as "Qué incluye" — or name the <ul> with aria-labelledby.

accessibility.contrast: Text: cream-dim ≥ 9.8:1 on every page and card surface in both themes (tightest: the light theme on surface-deep, 9.89:1). Check: accent-text ≥ 4.94:1 dark, ≥ 5.19:1 light — above the 3:1 asked of a graphic, though it carries no meaning on its own.
accessibility.focus: Not focusable. A link inside the text takes its own focus ring.
accessibility.screenReader: Announced as a list item inside "list, N items", then its text. The check is not announced, so the list's label must say what the rows have in common.

voice: A noun phrase that names what you get: "Entrevistas ilimitadas", "Historial y progreso completos".
Concrete over abstract: "Tu CV en manos del entrevistador" rather than "Personalización".
Sentence case, no final period, no exclamation mark.
Rows of one list share a grammatical shape, so they scan as one list.
limits: One line where possible: ≤ 48 characters. Two lines are the most; a row longer than that is a paragraph.
examples: La empresa a la que de verdad te postulas
Tu CV en manos del entrevistador

when: Listing what a plan or an offer includes: the pricing cards, the early-access offer.
A short list of things the reader gets, where every row is a yes.

whenNot.situation: Something the user ticks or unticks
whenNot.instead: a native checkbox (<input type="checkbox">).

whenNot.situation: Steps to follow in order
whenNot.instead: an ordered list (<ol>) with numbers; a check says done or included, not next.

whenNot.situation: Comparing what one plan has and another lacks
whenNot.instead: a table with a column per plan, so a missing feature is stated rather than implied by a missing row.

whenNot.situation: Plain bullets with no sense of included
whenNot.instead: a <ul> with a small dot, as the journey cards use.

do: Put it inside a <ul> with a label before it, such as "Qué incluye".
Keep rows of one list to the same shape and length.
Lay rows out with flex-col gap-3 on the list.
dont: Don't render a CheckItem outside a list.
Don't use a check for something that is not included.
Don't recolour the check to rank rows.

related.name: Badge
related.difference: A single status in a pill; CheckItem is one row of a list of what is included.

i18n.rtl: The check stays at the start of the row, which is the right edge in Arabic and Hebrew. The glyph itself is not mirrored.
i18n.textExpansion: Wraps under itself with the check aligned to the first line (items-start). Portuguese "A empresa para a qual você realmente se candidata" takes two lines at 320px.
i18n.formatting: None: any number in the text ("5 sustentaciones") is written by the caller.

behaviour: The same size at every width; long rows wrap and the check stays on the first line.
Spacing between rows belongs to the list (gap-3), not to the item.

designTool.placement: Only inside a <ul> (flex flex-col gap-3), usually in a pricing or offer card, below a label that says what the checks mean.

differences: Accepts className and native <li> attributes; the app's copy takes children only.
Wraps children in a single `min-w-0` span, so mixed inline content stays one flex item and can shrink; the app's copy lays each child out as its own flex item.

changes: The contract now names the class name of the difference: the system wraps the children in a min-w-0 span.
Nothing changes for a screen: the alternatives are named in plain words now — a native checkbox, an ordered list, a table, a plain list — because the system has no component for them.
First documented version, extracted from the product.

items.name: chip
items.title: Chip
items.description: A peach chip in mono caps: a fact, never a control.

contract.name: Chip
contract.summary: A peach chip in mono caps: a fact, never a control.

children.description: The fact: "LATAM", "HIPÓTESIS · PRIORIZACIÓN".

className.description: Extra classes, appended: the chip's own placement (a margin, a wrap). Not the fill and not the ink — a chip that changes them stops being a fact.

slots.name: children
slots.description: The fact, in caps.

states.name: default
states.description: A warm peach wash with the dark ink on it, in mono caps, rounded at 9px.

motion: None. The chip does not move; a chip that moved would look pressable.

accessibility.role: A <span>: a piece of text in a wash.
accessibility.contrast: The dark ink on the peach wash: over 12:1 in both themes, and the wash itself clears 3:1 against the card behind it.
accessibility.focus: Not focusable: a fact is read, not reached.
accessibility.screenReader: Reads the words in caps, like the rest of the text.

voice: A fact, in the instrument voice: caps, mono, a little tracking.
It names something and never instructs: "LATAM" names a region, "Recomendado" names a plan.
limits: 1–4 words, 28 characters at most; the chip wraps rather than truncates.

when: A fact about a product or a plan, next to the words it belongs to.
A row of what a plan includes, in one line each.

whenNot.situation: A status of the current screen
whenNot.instead: a Badge: the words carry the status, in the system's own voice.

whenNot.situation: Something the person can press
whenNot.instead: an Action: a chip is a fact, never a control.

whenNot.situation: A label of a block
whenNot.instead: a MonoLabel: the label is above the block, in the same voice.

do: Put the chip next to the words it qualifies, not on its own line.
Keep it to a fact the reader can verify: a region, a plan, a list of what is included.
dont: Don't put a price in it: the price is a sentence, and the sentence is what the reader compares.
Don't style it as a control: no border, no shadow, no hover.

related.name: Badge
related.difference: A status of the current screen, in the system's own voice. This is a fact about a product or a plan, in the peach.

related.name: MonoLabel
related.difference: The label above a block. This is a fact beside the words.

related.name: IconTile
related.difference: A square with a figure in it. This is a pill with words in it.

i18n.rtl: Nothing mirrors: the chip is symmetric and the words inside it are text.
i18n.textExpansion: The words wrap inside the chip and the chip grows with them; a German name of a plan is longer than a Spanish one and the chip says so.
i18n.formatting: None.

behaviour: Phones: 12px of padding on each side, in 12px mono caps.
From sm (640px): the same; the chip does not change with the width.
A chip too long for its row wraps its words rather than overflowing.

designTool.placement: Beside the words it qualifies, inside a Widget or a row of facts.

differences: Spreads every other <span> attribute (id, title, data-*); the app's copy accepts only children and className.
The fill and the ink are the chip's own tokens now, the same peach the app wrote as a literal colour.

changes: First documented version, taken from the product's own copy of the public site's chip.
The peach wash and its ink are tokens now, so the chip is a token the design tools can pick.

items.name: content-column
items.title: ContentColumn
items.description: The public site's one column: 1200px of content, the same gutters on every page.

contract.name: ContentColumn
contract.summary: The public site's one column: 1200px of content, the same gutters on every page.

children.description: The page's content: a band, a grid, a row of cards.

className.description: Extra classes, appended: the column's own layout (a grid, a flex row) and the padding of a band that is not the page's. Not a max-w-* — the ceiling is the same everywhere.

slots.name: children
slots.description: One page's worth of bands, in one column. Everything inside is as wide as the column allows.

states.name: default
states.description: The column is as wide as the window allows, up to 1200px, with 20px of gutter on a phone and 32px from 640px up.

motion: None. The column does not move; the page inside it scrolls.

accessibility.role: A generic <div> inside another <div>: the ceiling and the gutters, nothing more.
accessibility.contrast: None of its own: the column has no text and no surface beyond what the caller puts on it.
accessibility.focus: Not focusable itself. Focus moves through the content inside it, and nothing is trapped at the column's edge.
accessibility.screenReader: Adds nothing to what a screen reader reads: it is a generic container with no role and no name.

voice: None: the column holds content and never writes any of its own.
limits: Nothing: the column is layout.

when: The public site: every band of every public page sits in this column, so a card that moves from one page to another lands in the same place.
Any page whose content is one column and the same width everywhere.

whenNot.situation: A screen inside the signed-in app
whenNot.instead: PageBody: the app is the window, and it does not need a frame around it.

whenNot.situation: A band with its own vertical rhythm
whenNot.instead: Section: it owns the padding above and below the band.

whenNot.situation: A block of content inside the page
whenNot.instead: a Widget: the block, its own label and its own hairline.

do: Let the column fill the width it is given; the ceiling is there for a reason.
Keep one column per page: two columns in a row is a grid, and a grid needs a decision.
dont: Don't set a max-w-* on it: the ceiling is the column's, and a second one fights it.
Don't use it for the signed-in app; the app's screens are wider and tighter.

related.name: Section
related.difference: The band: it owns the vertical rhythm and centres a column of its own. This is the column without the band.

related.name: PageBody
related.difference: The app's container: wider, tighter gutters and a ceiling that follows the screen rather than the page.

related.name: Widget
related.difference: One block inside the column, with a hairline and its own padding.

i18n.rtl: Nothing mirrors: the column is symmetric and the page inside it handles its own direction.
i18n.textExpansion: Nothing changes: the column is a width, and the page inside it grows with its language.
i18n.formatting: None.

behaviour: Phones: 20px of gutter on each side, the column as wide as the window.
From sm (640px): 32px of gutter on each side.
Above 1200px the column stops growing and centres; the gutters stay.

designTool.placement: The outermost element of a public page. One per page, above the page's own bands.

differences: Spreads every other <div> attribute (id, aria-*, data-*); the app's copy accepts only children and className.

changes: First documented version, taken from the product's own copy of the public site's column.

items.name: eyebrow
items.title: Eyebrow
items.description: The short line in the accent above a heading or a value: it says where the reader is, the heading says what it means.

contract.name: Eyebrow
contract.summary: The short line in the accent above a heading or a value: it says where the reader is, the heading says what it means.

children.description: The kicker: a noun phrase of one to four words. Plain text; it is read as a paragraph just before the heading.

className.description: Extra classes, appended. For spacing and grid placement (lg:col-span-2) — not for colour, case or tracking.

slots.name: children
slots.description: Text only. No icons, no links: the eyebrow is a label, and anything you can press belongs elsewhere.

states.name: default
states.description: 16px semibold (text-sm in this scale) in accent-text, on its own line.

motion: None of its own. An eyebrow enters with the block around it, never separately.

accessibility.role:
paragraph (native

) — deliberately not a heading

aria.note: Do not add them. The heading that follows names the section; an eyebrow promoted to a heading gives the section two entries in the headings list.

Native attributes are spread onto the

; pass lang when the eyebrow is in a different language from the page, so it is pronounced correctly.

accessibility.contrast: accent-text on every page and card surface: ≥ 4.94:1 on the dark theme (tightest: surface-card) and ≥ 5.19:1 on the light one (surface-deep). On a surface-lift row inside a dark card it falls to 4.05:1 — keep it off lifted rows.
accessibility.focus: Not focusable.
accessibility.screenReader: Read as a plain paragraph just before the heading. Someone moving by headings skips it, so the heading must make sense without it.

voice: A noun phrase, not a sentence: "Precios", "Acta simulada", "Qué esperar".
It places; the heading says something. "Precios" over "Gratis para conseguir el trabajo. Después, al precio de tu país."
Sentence case, no final period, no colon, no exclamation mark.
If it needs a verb, it is the heading, not the eyebrow.
limits: 1–4 words; about 32 characters, so it stays on one line in a 320px phone's column. Longer translations wrap, and that is fine.

when: Above a landing section's heading, to place it: "Precios", "Acceso anticipado".
Above a value in a platform card: "Nivel" over the level, "Acta simulada" over the grade.
As the label of a group of controls inside a card that already sits under a page heading: "Apariencia", "Cuenta".

whenNot.situation: The name of a section or a page
whenNot.instead: a heading (an h2 inside Section, the title of PageHeader). The eyebrow goes above it, never in place of it.

whenNot.situation: A status or a mode on an item
whenNot.instead: Badge.

whenNot.situation: The label of a form field
whenNot.instead: Field, whose label is tied to its input.

whenNot.situation: A sentence of explanation
whenNot.instead: body text in cream-dim under the heading.

do: Pair it with a heading that says something.
One eyebrow per block.
Use className for spacing and grid placement only.
dont: Don't make it the only title of a section.
Don't set it in spaced capitals or another colour.
Don't end it with a period or a colon.

related.name: Badge
related.difference: A status on one item, in a pill; Eyebrow places a whole block.

i18n.textExpansion: Wraps like any paragraph and never truncates. German "Vom Vorstellungsgespräch zur Gehaltserhöhung" takes two lines at 320px.
i18n.formatting: None: the text is the caller's.

behaviour: The same size at every width (16px semibold).
Wraps onto a second line in a narrow column instead of truncating.

designTool.placement: Directly above a heading (landing sections) or above a value or a group inside a card (platform). Something must follow it: a heading, a number or the group it labels.

items.name: field
items.title: Field

contract.name: Field
contract.summary: A labelled form control: the name above it, the control, a hint below. The spacing of the three is the same in every form in the product.

label.description: The name of the control, in sentence case: "Tu nombre", "Correo". It names the control; it never describes it.

children.description: The control itself: an input, a select, a textarea. The component wraps whatever it is given and never renders a control of its own.

hint.description: One line under the control saying what it wants: "El jurado la lee antes de cada ensayo." Omitted, nothing renders.

htmlFor.description: The id of the control the label names. Leave it out when the control sits inside the label; pass it when the control is somewhere else in the tree.

className.description: Extra classes, appended. For layout — a field that spans more than its cell in a grid — not for restyling the label.

slots.name: children
slots.description: One control, with its own id and its own value. The Field brings the label and the spacing, not the control.

states.name: default
states.description: The label above the control in cream at 14px, medium weight; the hint under it in cream-faint at 14px; 8px between the three.

motion: None. The field does not move; the control inside it does whatever it does.

accessibility.role:
A generic
wrapping a

aria.note: The label names the control when htmlFor points at the control's id. Without it, the control has to sit inside the label.
The hint is a plain paragraph and is not wired to the control. When the hint is needed by a screen reader, point aria-describedby at its id.

accessibility.contrast: The label is cream on the surface it sits on, at least 13:1 in both themes; the hint is cream-faint, the lowest step the palette allows, 4.5:1 or more.
accessibility.focus: Not focusable itself. The control inside takes the focus ring (focus-ring): 2px accent with a 2px offset.
accessibility.targetSize: not interactive (the control inside brings its own target)
accessibility.screenReader: The label is read as the control's name when htmlFor points at it. The hint is read in the flow of the page, after the control, unless the control names it with aria-describedby.

voice: The label names the control in the person's own words: "Tu nombre", "Correo", "Título de tu tesis". Never "Campo" or "Input".
The hint says what the control wants, not what it is: "El jurado la lee antes de cada ensayo."
Tú form, sentence case, no final period, no exclamation marks.
limits: Label: 1–4 words, ≤ 30 characters, so it stays on one line above the control.
Hint: one line at 320px, about 60 characters. Anything longer belongs in the body of the screen.
examples: El jurado la lee antes de cada ensayo.

when: Every form control in the product that has a name: the name above, the control, the spacing.
A control with a hint: what it wants goes under it, where the eye already is.

whenNot.situation: A control that needs no name
whenNot.instead: the bare control, with its own placeholder or aria-label.

whenNot.situation: A choice between two or three options
whenNot.instead: a radio group with its own labels.

whenNot.situation: A question the person has to answer in their own words
whenNot.instead: a Notice above the form, not a hint under one field.

do: Give the control an id and pass it as htmlFor, so the label names it.
Keep the same order everywhere: label, control, hint.
dont: Don't use the hint for instructions about the form as a whole.
Don't restyle the label with className; the label's voice belongs to the system.

related.name: Notice
related.difference: Says something about the state of the screen; a Field names a control.

related.name: Panel
related.difference: The block a form can sit in.

i18n.rtl: The label, the control and the hint stack in the document's direction; the label stays above the control.
i18n.textExpansion: A German or Portuguese label runs about 30% longer: it wraps to two lines and the control moves down with it. The spacing between the three does not change.
i18n.formatting: None: the label and the hint come from the caller, already translated.

behaviour: Phones: the label, the control and the hint stack in a single column; a field that spans more than its cell in a grid keeps spanning it.
From sm up: the same stack. A field's width is the caller's, through className.

designTool.placement: Inside a form or a Panel, once per control. Never around a group of controls: that is a fieldset.

differences: None: the app's copy is this component, prop for prop.

changes: Nothing changes for a screen: the alternatives are named in plain words now — the bare control, a radio group — because the system has no component for them.

contract.name: IconTile
contract.summary: A small amber-tint square holding an icon or a number.

children.description: The icon or the figure that goes in the tile.

className.description: Extra classes, appended: the tile's own size when it has to grow with the icon inside it. Not the fill and not the colour.

slots.name: children
slots.description: An icon, or a figure in the instrument voice.

states.name: default
states.description: A 40px square with the accent's soft wash behind it and the accent's text colour in it.

motion: None. The tile does not move.

accessibility.role: A <span> with aria-hidden: a decoration next to words.

aria.note: The tile holds a number or an icon that the words beside it already carry. A screen reader that read both would say everything twice.

accessibility.contrast: The accent's text colour on its soft wash: over 4.5:1 in both themes.
accessibility.focus: Not focusable, and there is nothing inside it to focus.
accessibility.screenReader: Reads nothing: the tile is hidden, and the words beside it carry it.

voice: A figure in the instrument voice: "01", "02", "03".
An icon with no words of its own.
limits: One or two characters in the instrument voice; an icon at 16px.

when: A numbered row: the tile holds the number and the words beside it hold the step.
A row of icons that mark what a card is about.

whenNot.situation: A status the reader has to know

whenNot.situation: An icon that is the only content

items.name: mark
items.title: Mark
items.description: The isologo: Mocki the parrot as three shapes on the mustard tile, in the brand's fixed colours, legible down to 16px.

contract.name: Mark
contract.summary: The isologo: Mocki the parrot as three shapes on the mustard tile, in the brand's fixed colours, legible down to 16px.

size.description: Width and height in px, written as the SVG's width and height attributes. A className with h-/w- (for example h-[1.3em] w-[1.3em]) overrides it.

label.description: The accessible name. With a non-empty label the SVG becomes role="img" with that aria-label; without one (or with an empty or whitespace-only one) it is aria-hidden. Pass it only when the mark stands alone and nothing next to it already says the name. No default: decorative is the default.

className.description: Extra classes on the <svg>, appended after shrink-0. For sizing in em, a rounded corner that matches a shadow (rounded-[0.55rem] shadow-card), or margin — never for colour.

states.name: default
states.description: Decorative: aria-hidden, no role, not announced. The tile, crest, head, eye and beak in the brand colours.
states.trigger: Initial render, label omitted or empty.

states.name: named
states.description: Looks identical. Carries role="img" and the label as aria-label, so a screen reader announces it as an image with that name.

motion: None. The mark never animates: it is the one thing on the screen that stays put.

accessibility.role: none while decorative (aria-hidden); img when label is set

aria.note: Set to true when there is no label, so a mark beside the written name is not announced twice.
Set from label when it is non-empty. The text itself is the consumer's: "Mockio" is the brand name and is not translated.
Always set, so legacy browsers do not put the SVG in the tab order.
A mark used as the home link keeps label empty and names the link instead: <a aria-label="Mockio">.

accessibility.reducedMotion: Nothing to reduce: the mark has no motion.
accessibility.contrast: Brand colours, not tokens, so the figures are the same in both themes. The tile is ≥ 3:1 against every surface token (tightest: surface-card on dark, 3.0:1; 5.6:1 on the light page). The white head is 5.6:1 on the tile and the eye 14.4:1 on the head. The orange beak is 2.6:1 on the tile — it is a detail of the drawing, not what identifies it.
accessibility.focus: Never focusable. When the mark is a link, the link carries .focus-ring.
accessibility.screenReader: Silent by default. With label="Mockio" it is announced as "Mockio, image" (wording varies by reader).

voice: The label, when there is one, is the brand name and nothing else: "Mockio". Not "Logo de Mockio" — the role already says it is an image.
The name is never translated: "Mockio" in every locale, so the label is not a dictionary string.
limits: label: the brand name only, one word.

when: The product's corner of the app shell, beside or instead of the written name (the top bar at 30px).
Any place the brand must be recognisable in a square: an icon tile, a compact header.
Inside Wordmark, which composes it at the height of the name.

whenNot.situation: The brand needs to be read, not only recognised (landing nav, footer, sign-in)
whenNot.instead: Wordmark — the mark and the name as one lockup.

whenNot.situation: Showing the user's progress or a friendly face in an empty state, an error or a level-up
whenNot.instead: Mascot — the full illustrated Mocki, in one of its six stages.

whenNot.situation: A decorative background behind marketing copy
whenNot.instead: Backdrop. The mark is an identifier, not a pattern; never tile or repeat it.

do: Leave it decorative when the name is written next to it, and name the link instead.
Give the tile's corner to the shadow with a matching rounded class when you add shadow-card.
Keep it at 16px or larger: it is drawn to read at favicon size and no smaller.
dont: Don't recolour it with className, filters or currentColor: the colours are the brand.
Don't rotate, stretch, outline or mirror it, in any direction or locale.
Don't put text on top of it or crop the tile.

related.name: Wordmark

meta.description: One line under the title: what the screen is for, or the one fact that places it (a count, the thesis it is about). Clamped to one line with an ellipsis; the full text stays in the DOM and in a title tooltip. Omitted or empty, nothing renders.

actions.description: Controls at the end of the title row: one Action, or a few Badges that state the screen's mode. On a phone they wrap under the title.

compact.description: For a screen whose content is the point, like a call: on phones the title drops from 32px to 20px and the space above from 32px to 16px. From sm up the size and spacing match every other screen. The title is clamped to two lines at every width.

dense.description: For a workspace screen that has to hold its own: the title is 20px on a phone and 24px from sm up, and the space above it is 16px at every width. The body below it does not shrink. Use it when the screen is a list, not a moment.

width.description: The ceiling, the same values as PageBody's width. Pass the PageBody's value so the title starts where the content starts.

values.wide: max-w-[110rem]: the default, for every screen with a wide PageBody.
values.reading: max-w-3xl, centred: above a PageBody with width="reading".

slots.name: actions
slots.description: One Action (a solid one only when it is the screen's way forward, e.g. "Otra vez, sin miedo"), or Badges for the mode: "Práctica", "Turno 3 de 7". Never a row of three buttons.

states.name: default
states.description: The h1 at 32px (40px from sm), bold, tracking -0.028em; meta in cream-dim at 16px below it; actions bottom-aligned at the row's end. The title's measure is capped at 52rem and balanced across its lines, so it stays a heading on a wide window. No rule under it.

states.name: truncated
states.description: The meta is longer than one line at the current width: it stops at the end of the first line with an ellipsis. The full text is still in the DOM, so a screen reader reads all of it, and a mouse user sees it in the title tooltip on hover.
states.trigger: meta longer than one line at the current width: a 25-word thesis title at any width, or a meta over about 35 characters at 320px.

motion: None. The header is the fixed point a screen changes under; it never animates in.

accessibility.role: <header> containing heading level 1. Inside a <main> it is generic; outside any <main>, <article>, <aside>, <nav> or <section> it is a banner landmark

aria.note: The title is the page's only h1. One PageHeader per screen; headings below start at h2.

The app shell wraps PageHeader and PageBody in one <main>, so the header is not a second banner next to the shell's and the screen is a main landmark. The product's shell renders screens without a <main> today.
The meta's full text, for the hover tooltip when it is clamped. Same text as the content, so screen readers that read both announce it once.
Whatever is passed in actions brings its own name and role.

accessibility.contrast: On the shell's surface-deep ground: cream-bright title 18.8:1 (dark) and 17.3:1 (light); cream-dim meta 13.0:1 and 9.9:1.
accessibility.focus: Not focusable itself. The actions follow the title in source order, so they are the first stops in the screen's content after the shell's navigation.
accessibility.targetSize: not interactive (actions bring their own targets)
accessibility.screenReader: Announced as heading level 1 with the title, then the meta in full — the one-line clamp is visual only. On touch the clamped part of the meta cannot be revealed (the tooltip needs a pointer), so nothing a person needs to act on may live only in the meta.

voice: The title names the screen in one to four words, sentence case, no period: "Mi tesis", "Tu camino", "Tus postulaciones".
Possessives in the tú form where the screen is the person's own: "Tu informe", "Tu camino".
Meta is one short sentence that says what the screen is for, or one fact: "Súbela una vez. El jurado la lee antes de cada ensayo.", "12 completadas".
No exclamation marks; meta never repeats the title.
limits: Title: ≤ 40 characters so it stays on one line at 320px (two at most).
Title measure: 52rem. The title wraps at that measure, not at the width of the window — a heading that can run the full width of a desktop screen stops being a heading and becomes a line of text.
Meta: one line. About 35 characters fit at 320px, about 45 at 390px and about 70 from 640px; anything longer is cut, so the point goes in the first 35 characters and instructions go in the body.
examples: Súbela una vez. El jurado la lee antes de cada ensayo.
Equivócate aquí, no en la entrevista

when: At the top of every screen in the signed-in app, once, directly above its PageBody.
compact for a screen whose content needs the height on a phone: the live call.
dense for a workspace screen that is a list rather than a moment: the thesis workspace.

whenNot.situation: A marketing page's headline
whenNot.instead: the hero's own h1, then Sections with h2.

whenNot.situation: A heading inside the screen
whenNot.instead: an h2 in a Panel.

whenNot.situation: Instructions or a long description of the screen
whenNot.instead: a Panel in the PageBody; meta is cut to one line.

whenNot.situation: A status message (an error, a saved confirmation)
whenNot.instead: Notice, in the PageBody.

do: Pass the same width to PageHeader and PageBody.
Put the point of the meta in its first 35 characters: that is what a 320px phone shows.
Keep one Action in actions, and make it solid only when it is the screen's way forward.
dont: Don't render a second PageHeader (or any other h1) on a screen.
Don't put something the person must read to act in meta: on touch, the clamped part cannot be revealed.
Don't draw a rule or a background under the header.

related.name: PageBody
related.difference: The content container under it, with the same gutters and ceiling.

related.name: Badge
related.difference: Goes in actions to state the screen's mode ("Práctica", "Modo estrés").

related.name: Action
related.difference: Goes in actions: at most one, the screen's way forward.

i18n.rtl: The row follows the document direction: the title starts at the right and the actions move to the left end. The meta's ellipsis lands at the line's end (the left in RTL).
i18n.textExpansion: The title wraps (compact clamps it at two lines); the meta is clamped at one line, so a Portuguese or German meta 30–40% longer than the Spanish shows less of itself rather than growing the header. Actions wrap under the title when the row runs out.
i18n.formatting: None: title and meta come formatted from the caller (a count through Intl, a date through the app's formatter).

behaviour: Phones: 16px gutters; 32px above (16px when compact or dense); title 32px (20px when compact or dense); actions wrap onto their own line under the title when the row runs out of room.
From sm (640px): 24px gutters, title 40px, 32px above in both modes. With dense the title stays at 24px.
From lg (1024px): 40px gutters, 40px above. The row stops at the width's ceiling and centres; the title stops at 52rem, so a long heading wraps there instead of running the width of the window.

designTool.placement: The first child of the screen's <main> (provided by the app shell), directly above PageBody. One per screen.

differences: The title is light (`font-light`) in the app's copy and bold (`font-bold`) here, with its leading and tracking to match. The weight is the app's call: a light heading on the dark ground is quieter, and the app is the one people read.

The meta renders on one line (`line-clamp-1`) with the full text in a title attribute. The app's copy lets it wrap (`text-pretty`) inside a 46rem measure (`max-w-[46rem]`), so on the thesis screen a 25-word thesis title becomes the longest block of the header; this is the minimalist redesign's decision, ahead of the product.
Adds width ("wide" | "reading") to match PageBody's: the reading ceiling is `max-w-3xl` here, and the app's copy has no width prop at all, so its title does not line up with a narrower body.

changes: The contract now names the class names of the difference: the title's weight, the measure the meta wraps in and the reading ceiling.
Nothing changes for a screen: the alternatives are named in plain words now — the hero's own h1, an h2 in a Panel — because the system has no component for them.
New dense prop: a small title and 16px above it at every width, for the workspace screens that are a list rather than a moment. The app's copy already had it; the contract now says so.
The title's measure is capped at 52rem and balanced across its lines, so a heading cannot run the width of a desktop window.
First documented version, extracted from the product's app shell.
Meta clamped to one line with the full text in a title attribute.
width prop, matching PageBody.

items.name: panel
items.title: Panel
items.description: The surface every card, block and sheet sits on: a rounded fill with the card shadow, or glass over imagery. No padding, no states.

contract.name: Panel
contract.summary: The surface every card, block and sheet sits on: a rounded fill with the card shadow, or glass over imagery. No padding, no states.

children.description: The panel's content. Panel adds no padding: give it p-6 sm:p-8 for a block, p-5 for a row, so the content clears the rounded corners.

variant.description: Which surface. Picks the fill and the edge; the radius and the clipping are the same for all three.

values.card: bg-surface-card + shadow-card. The lighter fill on the dark theme (#1C1C1E); white on the light one. For panels side by side in a grid: pricing tiers, settings sections, list rows.
values.raised: bg-surface-raised + shadow-card. A step darker than card on the dark theme (#161618), identical to card on the light one. For one block on the page ground: an upload step, an empty state, a wait.
values.glass: .liquid-glass: near-transparent with a 4px backdrop blur and a gradient edge on dark and inside .on-media; a white sheet with a hairline on the light theme. The only surface allowed over video. On a plain page the product uses it for errors (the message of a screen that failed to load, on five screens) and for two tabbed sheets (the account tab of the settings screen, the plan of the billing screen).

className.description: Extra classes, appended. Padding, layout (flex, grid, gap), width and a selection ring (ring-2 ring-accent). Not a background, border or radius — that is a variant.

id.description: Native id, passed through. For a panel a tab or a link has to point at (aria-controls, #anchor).

role.description: Native role, passed through. region (with aria-labelledby), tabpanel, status for a wait, alert for a failure. Leave it off for a plain card.

aria-labelledby.description: Native, passed through. The id of the heading or tab that names the panel; required with role="region" and role="tabpanel".

slots.name: children
slots.description: Anything: a heading (h2 on an app screen, h3 inside a landing Section), body copy, Actions, a form. One idea per panel. A group inside it is an inset well (rounded-2xl bg-surface-lift p-4), not a second Panel.

states.name: default
states.description: The variant's fill and edge, rounded-card (1.25rem), overflow hidden. Panel has no other state: hover, focus and selection belong to whatever the caller wraps around or adds.

motion: None of its own. A panel enters with the block around it, never separately.
A caller's hover:shadow-lift is a box-shadow transition; keep it for panels inside something pressable.

accessibility.role: none of its own (a plain <div>); the caller passes region, tabpanel, status or alert when the panel is one

aria.note: Only when the panel means something as a whole: tabpanel under a tablist, status around a wait, alert around a failure, region for a named block in the landmarks list.
Points at the heading or tab that names the panel. Required with region and tabpanel; a region with no name is not a landmark.
Every other <div> attribute is spread onto the surface.

accessibility.reducedMotion: Nothing moves, so nothing changes. A caller's hover:shadow-lift keeps fading under reduce, because box-shadow is on the system's list of transitions that carry no movement.
accessibility.contrast: Ink on every surface clears AA in both themes. Dark: cream-bright 16.3:1, cream-dim 11.6:1, cream-faint 7.3:1 and accent-text 4.94:1 on card (the tightest); raised and glass are higher. Light: cream-dim 10.5:1, cream-faint 5.2:1 on white. Over footage the picture sets the contrast: .on-media pins the ink to cream and the caller darkens the footage. The panel's own edge is decoration (card on surface-deep is 1.15:1 on dark, 1.09:1 on light), so nothing may depend on seeing it.
accessibility.focus: Not focusable and has no ring. overflow-hidden clips anything past the rounded edge, so keep at least 4px (in practice p-5 or more) between a control and the edge or its 2px ring and 2px offset are cut.
accessibility.screenReader: Nothing is announced for the surface. A plain panel is just its content; with a role it is announced as that role and its name.

voice: A panel's first line says what it is for, as a heading or a plain sentence: "Sube tu tesis", "Sesión iniciada en este dispositivo."
Body copy in the tú form, sentence case, no exclamation marks; a wait says what is happening and how long: "Leyendo tu tesis… puede tardar hasta dos minutos."
One primary Action per panel at most, and it repeats nothing the heading already said.
limits: One idea per panel: a heading, up to three short lines of body, one primary Action.
Body text at max-w-prose (65ch) inside wide panels, so a line never runs the full 110rem.
examples: Leyendo tu tesis… puede tardar hasta dos minutos.
Agrega el puesto para el que te estás preparando.

when: Any block of content that belongs together on a page: a step, a form section, an empty state, a wait, a tier.
A grid of equal items: give them all variant="card" and h-full so the row lines up.
Content over video or photography: variant="glass" inside .on-media.
A whole screen that failed to load: variant="glass" with role="alert" on the message.

whenNot.situation: A card the person presses as a whole (a session row, a nav tile)
whenNot.instead: a link or button styled with the card tokens itself (focus-ring rounded-2xl bg-surface-card shadow-card hover:shadow-lift). A Panel has no hover, focus or pressed state.

whenNot.situation: A group inside a panel
whenNot.instead: an inset well: rounded-2xl bg-surface-lift p-4. A Panel inside a Panel doubles the edge and the radius.

whenNot.situation: A one-line message about the screen's state
whenNot.instead: Notice, which carries the icon and the tone.

whenNot.situation: A card that opens and closes
whenNot.instead: a <details> element with the card surface.

whenNot.situation: Page gutters and width
whenNot.instead: PageBody inside the app, Section on a marketing page.

do: Use card for siblings in a grid and raised for a single block on the page.
Give the panel its padding through className: p-6 sm:p-8.
Give a wait role="status" and a failure role="alert".
Mark the recommended one of a set with ring-2 ring-accent, not a glow.
dont: Don't put hover:shadow-lift on a panel nothing happens on — it promises a press.
Don't nest a Panel in a Panel.
Don't recolour it with bg-* or border-*; pick the variant.
Don't reach for glass on a plain page for a grid of ordinary cards: on the dark theme it is near-transparent and reads as empty; use card.

related.name: Section
related.difference: A marketing page's band of rhythm and width; Panels sit inside it.

related.name: PageBody
related.difference: The app screen's container; Panels sit inside it.

related.name: Backdrop
related.difference: A decorative field behind a hero, aria-hidden and empty; Panel holds content.

i18n.rtl: Nothing to mirror: the surface is symmetric. Content inside follows the document direction.
i18n.textExpansion: The panel grows in height with its content and takes its width from the caller's layout, so longer Portuguese or German copy wraps and the panel gets taller. Nothing is truncated.
i18n.formatting: None: the panel renders no text of its own.

behaviour: No breakpoints of its own: radius, fill and edge are the same at every width.
Padding steps up with the caller's className (p-6 → sm:p-8); grids of panels collapse to one column on phones (grid gap-5 lg:grid-cols-2).

designTool.placement: Inside PageBody on an app screen or inside a Section on a marketing page, alone or in a grid. Never inside another Panel.

differences: Spreads every other <div> attribute onto the surface. The app's copy accepts only id, role and aria-labelledby, so a panel there cannot carry aria-busy, aria-label or data-* attributes.

changes: Nothing changes for a screen: the alternatives are named in plain words now — a link styled with the card tokens, an inset well, a details element — because the system has no component for them.
First documented version, extracted from the product.
Native <div> attributes are passed through.

items.name: premium-mark
items.title: PremiumMark
items.description: The gold crown on an option that belongs to the paid plan, named for screen readers; the option itself stays usable.

contract.name: PremiumMark
contract.summary: The gold crown on an option that belongs to the paid plan, named for screen readers; the option itself stays usable.

label.description: The mark's accessible name and its tooltip, read instead of the crown. A blank string falls back to the default, so the mark is never an unnamed image.

className.description: Extra classes, appended. For placement (ms-auto at the end of a row, an absolute corner on a thumbnail) — not for size or colour.

states.name: default
states.description: A 20px circle in premium-soft with a 12px filled crown in premium.

motion: None. The mark is static wherever it appears; the paid plan's one moving flourish is ShimmerText in the top bar.

accessibility.role: img (role="img" on a <span>), named by label

aria.note: Set from label, so the crown is announced as a word, never as "image".
The SVG inside is hidden; the span carries the name.
The same text as a tooltip for mouse users. Touch and keyboard users do not get it, so the name must not be the only place an important condition is explained.

accessibility.contrast: The crown is a graphic: premium on premium-soft is 8.82:1 on the dark theme and 4.17:1 on the light one, above the 3:1 asked of non-text. The soft circle itself is a wash, not a boundary, and needs no contrast.
accessibility.focus: Not focusable. Inside a link, tab or button it adds to that control's accessible name and takes no focus of its own.
accessibility.screenReader: Read as its label. Inside a control the label joins the control's name: a tab is named "En el trabajo Premium" and a rail link "Tu contexto Del plan pago".

voice: The plan's name or where the option lives: "Premium", "Del plan pago".
A name, not a refusal: never "Bloqueado" or "No disponible".
Sentence case, no period.
limits: 1–4 words. It is heard, and seen only as a tooltip, so brevity is for the ear.

when: Next to any option the free plan cannot use: a rail entry, a practice tab, a share template, a section of the report.
Wherever the option appears, the same mark — so it is learnt once.

whenNot.situation: Saying the paid plan is active for this person
whenNot.instead: ShimmerText in the top bar's "Premium" chip.

whenNot.situation: A status of the current screen
whenNot.instead: Badge.

whenNot.situation: Explaining what the paid plan adds
whenNot.instead: a sentence beside the option with a link to the plans ("Ver los planes").

do: Keep the marked option visible and pressable; let the press explain or open the plans.
Put it at the end of the option's label (ms-auto in a full-width row).
Use the default label unless the place needs "Del plan pago".
dont: Don't disable an option because it carries the mark.
Don't use the crown or the gold for anything else.
Don't resize or recolour it through className.

related.name: ShimmerText
related.difference: Says the paid plan is on, once, in the top bar; PremiumMark marks each option that needs it.

related.name: Badge
related.difference: States a status in visible words; PremiumMark is a crown with a spoken name.

i18n.rtl: The crown is not mirrored. Place it with logical utilities (ms-auto, not ml-auto) so it sits at the end of the row in both directions.
i18n.textExpansion: Fixed 20px whatever the language; only the spoken label and the tooltip grow.
i18n.formatting: None.

behaviour: The same 20px at every width; shrink-0, so a wrapping label never squeezes it.
Where a label is hidden at small widths (the collapsed rail), hide the mark with it, as the product does with hidden lg:inline-grid.

designTool.placement: At the end of an option's label — inside a rail link, a tab, a card header or the corner of a template thumbnail.

differences: label is optional and defaults to "Premium" (the product's es copy of premium.mark); the app's copy requires it.
A blank label falls back to the default instead of rendering an image with no name.

changes: Nothing changes for a screen: the alternative is named in plain words now — a sentence beside the option — because the system has no component for it.
First documented version, extracted from the product.

items.name: screen-frame
items.title: ScreenFrame
items.description: A piece of the product, drawn as the product draws it: a window with a hairline and the interface inside.

contract.name: ScreenFrame
contract.summary: A piece of the product, drawn as the product draws it: a window with a hairline and the interface inside.

children.description: The interface itself: a transcript, a card, a row of the real product.

className.description: Extra classes, appended: the frame's own size and the padding of the interface inside it. Not the fill and not the edge.

dark.description: The call is always dark, as a video call is, whatever the theme.

slots.name: children
slots.description: The product, drawn as the product draws it. The frame clips what overflows it, so the content inside is laid out for the width it gets.

states.name: default
states.description: The frame is a card-coloured window with a hairline around it, and the interface inside is padded by the caller.

states.name: dark
states.description: The ground is the media ground, so the window reads as a lit screen in either theme and the ink inside stays light.

motion: None. The frame does not move; the interface inside it does whatever it does.

accessibility.role: A generic <div> with aria-hidden: the frame is a picture of the product.

aria.note: The frame is hidden from assistive technology. The page says the same thing in words next to it, and a screen reader that read both would say everything twice.

accessibility.contrast: None of its own: the frame has no text of its own beyond what the caller puts inside it.
accessibility.focus: Not focusable, and nothing inside it can be reached: the frame is a picture.
accessibility.screenReader: Reads nothing: the whole frame is hidden, and the page's words carry it.

voice: None: the frame holds the product and never writes any of its own.
limits: Nothing: the frame is layout.

when: The public site: a piece of the product shown as the product draws it, next to the words that say what it is.
Any place where the interface itself is the argument: a transcript, a card, the call.

whenNot.situation: A real screen of the signed-in app
whenNot.instead: PageBody: the app is the window, and it does not need a frame around it.

whenNot.situation: A card of content with words in it
whenNot.instead: a Widget: the frame is for the interface, not for copy.

whenNot.situation: A video
whenNot.instead: nothing: the frame is a window, and a video brings its own.

Say in words next to it what the frame shows, because the frame itself is silent.
dont: Don't put anything inside that has to be read or pressed: it is hidden from everyone but the eye.
Don't use it to frame a whole page; an InsetFrame is the frame of a page.

related.name: Widget

related.name: InsetFrame

related.name: PageBody
related.difference: The app's screen. This is a picture of the product, on the public site.

i18n.textExpansion: Nothing changes: the frame is a window and the interface inside it grows with its language.
i18n.formatting: None.

behaviour: Phones: the frame is as wide as the column allows, and the interface inside is padded by the caller.
From sm (640px): the same, with the caller's own padding.
The frame never scrolls: what overflows it is clipped.

designTool.placement: Inside a band of the public site, next to the words that explain it. Never around a whole page.

items.name: section
items.title: Section
items.description: A band of a marketing page: owns the vertical rhythm and side gutters, bleeds its background to both edges and centres content in one column.

contract.name: Section
contract.summary: A band of a marketing page: owns the vertical rhythm and side gutters, bleeds its background to both edges and centres content in one column.

children.description: The band's content: usually an Eyebrow, an h2 and what the heading introduces. It sits in a centred max-w-7xl (80rem) column.

className.description: Extra classes for the outer <section>: the band's background (bg-surface-base, bg-surface-deep) and positioning (relative). They land on the full-bleed element, not on the content column, so a grid or a gap belongs on a <div> inside.

id.description: The anchor the landing nav scrolls to ("pricing", "features"). Also the target of a skip or in-page link.

aria-labelledby.description: Native, passed through. The id of the band's h2; it names the <section> so it becomes a region landmark a screen-reader user can jump to.

slots.name: children
slots.description: The band's content. Opens with its heading — an h2 (the page's h1 lives in the hero), optionally preceded by an Eyebrow — then the body: Panels in a grid, a list, a chart. Narrower blocks set their own max-w-* and mx-auto inside.

states.name: default
states.description: py-20 / px-4 on phones, sm:py-28 / sm:px-6, lg:py-36 / lg:px-10. The background in className reaches both window edges; content is centred at max-w-7xl. Section has no other state.

motion: None of its own. The blocks inside bring their own entrance as they scroll into view; the band itself never moves.

accessibility.role: generic (<section> without an accessible name); region when aria-labelledby names it

aria.note: Point it at the band's h2 (give the h2 an id). Without a name a <section> is announced as nothing and does not appear in the landmarks list.
Spread onto the <section>. Prefer aria-labelledby over aria-label, so the name is the visible heading.

accessibility.reducedMotion: Nothing moves, so nothing changes. The motion inside belongs to the blocks that come with it, and they handle reduced motion themselves.
accessibility.contrast: Section draws no ink. On the backgrounds landing bands use, the ink tokens clear AA in both themes: on surface-deep cream-bright is 18.8:1 and cream-faint 7.8:1 (dark), 17.3:1 and 5.1:1 (light); on surface-base (black / white) they are higher.
accessibility.focus: Not focusable. With an id it can be the target of an in-page link; the browser moves the reading position there.
accessibility.screenReader: With aria-labelledby: announced as a region with the heading's text, and listed among landmarks. Without it: not announced; the heading inside is what a screen-reader user navigates by.

voice: The heading is one plain claim, sentence case, ending in a period when it is a sentence: "Gratis para conseguir el trabajo. Después, al precio de tu país."
The Eyebrow above it names the topic in two or three words: "Precios", "De la entrevista al aumento".
Body under the heading in the tú form, concrete, no exclamation marks: "XP por cada entrevista, una racha que perdona un mal día, misiones semanales e insignias que te ganas."
limits: Heading: one sentence or two short ones, ≤ 90 characters, text-balance so it breaks evenly.
Intro paragraph: ≤ 2 sentences, in a max-w-2xl column.
One idea per band; if a band needs two headings it is two bands.
examples: Gratis para conseguir el trabajo. Después, al precio de tu país.
Cada conversación de un trabajo remoto, ensayada antes de que cuente.
Un hábito que vas a querer mantener

when: Each band of the landing or another marketing page: features, pricing, how it works, the habit loop.
Alternating backgrounds down a page: give consecutive bands bg-surface-base and bg-surface-deep through className.

whenNot.situation: A screen inside the signed-in app
whenNot.instead: PageBody (with PageHeader above it): tighter gutters, a wider ceiling, no marketing rhythm.

whenNot.situation: A block inside a band (a tier, a feature card)
whenNot.instead: Panel, inside the Section.

whenNot.situation: The hero at the top of the page
whenNot.instead: the hero's own full-height layout over a Backdrop; it is not a padded band.

whenNot.situation: Laying out the content in columns through className
whenNot.instead: a <div className="grid …"> inside the Section; className reaches the outer band, not the column.

do: Give the band an id the nav can scroll to and name it with aria-labelledby on its h2.

speed.description: Seconds the light takes to cross the text once. Higher is slower. Zero, negative or non-finite values fall back to 2.4.

pause.description: Seconds the text stays still between two sweeps. 0 runs them back to back; negative or non-finite values count as 0.

states.name: disabled
states.description: No sweep and no gradient: plain accent-text in the same inline-block box.

motion: One cycle lasts speed + pause seconds and repeats for as long as the component is mounted: the text stays still for `pause` seconds (4 by default), then the light crosses it in `speed` seconds (2.4 by default) at a constant rate (linear). The first sweep therefore comes `pause` seconds after mount.

Only background-position animates, from one keyframe; per-instance timing comes from an inline background-size and animation-duration. It repaints the text's own box each frame and never triggers layout — keep it to one instance per view.
Right-to-left: under :dir(rtl) the animation runs in reverse, so the light travels right to left, in reading order. There each cycle opens with the sweep and the pause follows.
Reduced motion: no sweep and no gradient; the text is drawn in the base colour.

accessibility.role: generic (native <span>) holding real text

aria.note: Deliberately absent. The visible text is the DOM text, so it is read, translated, found and selected as written.

accessibility.reducedMotion: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the sweep never runs and the text is plain accent-text. useReducedMotion() from framer-motion chooses the static branch when the component mounts; a prefers-reduced-motion media query in its own <style> covers a server render and a setting changed while the page is open. No MotionConfig provider is needed.
accessibility.contrast: Every pixel is a mix of accent-text (the base) and cream-bright (the light), and in both themes the mix is never lower in contrast than the base. On the product's chip (accent-soft) that is ≥ 4.65:1 dark and ≥ 4.92:1 light at every frame; on page and card surfaces ≥ 4.94:1 dark and ≥ 5.19:1 light. Not for a surface-lift row in a dark card (4.05:1) or an accent fill (1.47:1). Selected text is drawn in accent-ink on accent (≥ 5:1). Forced-colours mode drops the gradient and draws CanvasText; print, and a browser that cannot clip a background to text, draw plain accent-text, so it never renders or prints blank.
accessibility.focus: Not focusable.
accessibility.screenReader: Read as its text, exactly as written; the light is not announced, and nothing is hidden or relabelled. A sighted reader sees the sweep; a screen-reader user loses nothing by not hearing it.

voice: A name, not a message: the plan's name as the product writes it, "Premium".
